record: Rule-6 mutants for the session pair's provider-statement check in session-prompt after review R-PR406-SESSION-TOOL-STATEMENT-1 (syzygy-up98). U1-U9 re-run from the first record (session-prompt-tool-statement-mutants-2026-10-08.json; U7's fragment follows the gate line's new form). U10-U11: N1, two in-force statements for the session pair refuse at the gate as ambiguous, and the reason does not call that no statement in force. U12: N3, the design kind is refused at the statement too. R1: E1, the reviewer's mutant (the early gate skips review sessions and a late gate refuses after writePacket), applied as one span replacement so the single-occurrence runner can apply it; it survived the round-1 tests (raw, E1) and is killed here. A separate probe with only R1 applied showed the failing assertion is the state-root comparison (review.test.ts line 673), which lists the reviews/fidelity-packet-<sha>/ entries R1 writes. The run was made on branch fix/session-tool-review-notes at the subject commit, the parent of the commit that adds this record; a rebase-merge leaves it reachable from no ref, so the old/new fragments and the file digests are the re-runnable form. Not authority.
runner: single-occurrence textual replacement of `old` by `new` in `file`, then `npx vitest run --project <project> <testFiles>`; killed = at least one failed test; file restored from git after each run

mutants.note: session-prompt runs the session pair's statement check
a run relying on no statement (non-governed) needs none for the session pair
a run relying on a statement checks the session pair
the gate names the session's tool, not the run's declared tool
the classes are the session pair's statement's
the session pair's statement lists every class the run's lists
an absent statement (none, withdrawn, not yet in force) refuses
the session pair takes the run's declared provider
the subset runs from the run's classes into the session statement's, not the other way
N1: two in-force statements for the session pair refuse as ambiguous at the gate

mutants.old: statement.state === 'absent' ? 'has no per-project statement in force'
mutants.new: true ? 'has no per-project statement in force'
mutants.note: N1: the ambiguous refusal does not say no statement is in force

mutants.new: if (unstated !== null && request.kind !== 'design') return refuse('statement', unstated);
mutants.note: N3: the design kind is refused at the statement too
E1 (reviewer mutant R1): a gate that refuses only after the review packet is written under reviews/
